subject: Oceanography
title: Blue Carbon
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Blue Carbon.

hook.text: Mangroves, seagrasses, and salt marshes store carbon 40 times faster per hectare than tropical forests.

buildup.text: These coastal ecosystems trap sediment and organic matter—building carbon-rich soil over millennia.

discovery.text: This 'blue carbon' stays locked in waterlogged soils for thousands of years—far longer than forest carbon.

twist.text: When these habitats are destroyed, stored carbon is released—turning a carbon sink into a carbon source.

climax.text: We've lost 50% of mangroves and 30% of seagrasses—releasing centuries of stored carbon.

punchline.text: Coastal wetlands are climate heroes—losing them turns allies into enemies.

quiz.question: Why is blue carbon so effective?
options: Coastal ecosystems store carbon 40x faster than tropical forests
